base_setup_commands: DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq build-essential gcc g++ make cmake bison flex gawk gperf libncurses5-dev gcc-arm-none-eabi git curl ninja-build
setup_runtime_commands: pip3 install --user -q kconfiglib || apt-get install -y -qq python3-kconfiglib || true
pip3 install --user -q pexpect==4.8.0 pytest==6.2.5 pytest-repeat==0.9.1 pytest-json==0.4.0 pytest-ordering==0.6 pyserial==3.5 || true

prepare_commands: pip3 install --user -q kconfiglib || apt-get install -y -qq python3-kconfiglib || true
pip3 install --user -q pexpect==4.8.0 pytest==6.2.5 pytest-repeat==0.9.1 pytest-json==0.4.0 pytest-ordering==0.6 pyserial==3.5 || true
runtime_profile.notes: NuttX uses a Make-based build system with Kconfig for configuration. The apps repository must be cloned separately. Python kconfiglib is used for Kconfig parsing as an alternative to C-based kconfig-frontends. The pysim_cm7 configuration (added by fix.patch) enables simulator-based testing without hardware.

notes: Apache NuttX is a POSIX-compliant RTOS for embedded systems. This environment supports building NuttX with the nucleo-h745zi board configuration. The base image is Ubuntu 22.04 matching the project's CI Dockerfile. System packages include ARM GCC toolchain for cross-compilation. Python packages (pytest, pexpect, pyserial) are installed using pip3 --user for Ubuntu 22.04 compatibility (pip 22.0.2 does not support --break-system-packages which was added in pip 23.0+ per PEP 668). The setup_runtime.sh script clones the nuttx-apps repository before configure.sh and configures NuttX with the nsh_cm7 configuration. The pysim_cm7 configuration is available only after applying fix.patch.
